title: Feedback Frequency
hook: I was checking my conversion rate once a month. By then the damage was already done.
statement: The more often you check what matters, the faster you grow. As long as you act on it.
explainer: A metric you check monthly gives you twelve chances a year to fix things. Check it daily and you catch problems while they're still tiny.
sop: List your key metrics and how often you check each.
Rate the Frequency of your checks, 1 to 10. Daily is a 10.
Move your most important, least checked metric to weekly or daily.
Rate your Adjustment from 1 to 10. Do you act on what you see?
If Adjustment stays low, the problem is follow-through. Fix that next.
equation_example: Frequency 9, Adjustment 4. 9 × 4 = 36 out of 100. You're checking a lot but barely changing anything. Higher means checks turn into real fixes. Lower means you check rarely or do nothing with it.
question: Name one metric you check monthly that you should be checking every day.
closing_statement: Checking more only helps if you act on it.
caption:
Principle Nº 165: Feedback Frequency
